label: Yubico.YubiKit.YubiOtp.StaticPasswordSlotConfiguration :: private void Initialize(ReadOnlySpan<byte> scanCodes)
reason: String translation validates every character before allocating its byte array, then Initialize copies into fixed/uid/key with zeroed and finally-cleared stack scratch; its translated intermediate is cleared even on Initialize failure. Raw input is copied without clearing caller source. Core translator supplies character mapping only; neither overload uses ConsoleCredentialReader. Layout rendering and old-firmware length remain qualified rather than universal guarantees.

label: Yubico.YubiKit.YubiOtp.ConfigState :: public ConfigState(ReadOnlySpan<byte> statusBytes)
reason: The constructor copies version scalars into FirmwareVersion and decodes touch flags little-endian; it retains no status-memory alias. Accessors gate against raw status version with major-zero allowance. Trigger flags describe keyboard activation, not RequireTouch. Default struct construction leaves FirmwareVersion null; callers in reviewed session paths construct from status, and default-value hardening is a separate applet representation question rather than a new boundary acceptance.

label: Yubico.YubiKit.YubiOtp.SlotConfiguration :: protected void SetHmacKey(ReadOnlySpan<byte> hmacKey, ushort initialMovingFactor)
reason: Private fixed/uid/key storage copies source, GetConfig makes an independent 52-byte block and complements CRC, and Dispose clears only the three private arrays. Invalid new-code validation follows secret copying; invalid current-code validation can occur before WriteConfig's try. SetHmacKey stack UID is explicitly initialized and cleared. Flag setters are not all disposed-guarded. Retain OTP-IMP-003/006/007 and distinguish config lifetime from protocol exchange drain.

label: Yubico.YubiKit.YubiOtp.UnitTests.SlotConfigurationTests :: [Fact] public void StaticPassword_FromString_CopiesOwnedScanCodesBeforeZeroing()
reason: Complete tests check literal offsets, zero filler/RFU, exact key splits, flag defaults/toggles/masks, erroneous current IMF encoding, static scan-code distribution and string/raw equality. The injected translation factory asserts actual intermediate clearing on success/failure; raw source remains unchanged. AssertValidCrc shares production helper and the older Dispose-named test only checks rejection. Preserve existing accurate comments; independent CRC/device and exception cleanup proposals remain separate.

label: Yubico.YubiKit.YubiOtp.UnitTests.SlotConfigurationEncapsulationTests :: [Fact] public void Dispose_ZeroesAllConfigurationBuffers()
reason: Reflection tests retain actual private fixed/UID/key arrays, fill them, dispose and assert all zero. Guard tests check meaningful field-size messages but are not independent memory or firmware oracles. Unlike the older Dispose test this is actual owned-array zero observation by source assertion.

label: Yubico.YubiKit.YubiOtp.UnitTests.IYubiKeyExtensionsTransportTests :: [Fact] public async Task CreateYubiOtpSessionAsync_DefaultBothTransports_PicksSmartCard()
reason: SelectionProbe records requested type then throws, so it checks selection only. FallbackProbe holds default/explicit SmartCard and asserts a single attempt/no HID fallback. The FailingOtpConnection helper is not actually opened by those held-SmartCard tests; their no-disposal assertion does not exercise post-open initialization cleanup. Shared Core tests retain that mechanism's ownership.

label: Yubico.YubiKit.YubiOtp.UnitTests.YubiOtpSessionLinuxCrossLayerTests :: [Theory] [InlineData(true)] [InlineData(false)] public async Task PublicHmac_TerminalPresenceOutcomeBelongsToAppletCrcValidation(bool validCrc)
reason: The production Linux slot/device/native owner is used over fake feature seam. Held first GET distinguishes invocation return from completion; sequential borrowed sessions leave close count zero until connection disposal. Touch cancellation remains pending until held dummy SET returns, then serial recovers; CRC literal vectors determine applet Completed/Failed. Sent-frame CRC still uses production ChecksumUtils. Held creation's finally releases a gate but success-only first-session disposal can be skipped by an assertion failure; record this under existing test cleanup concern rather than claim all-path drain.
